title: Hold down a small engine and pull its recoil starter fast over the full stroke
instruction: Hold the engine down by its top pad with one arm, and with the other pull the yellow starter handle out fast over its full 30 cm, in under half a second. The engine must not shift more than 10 cm.
context: Anyone who starts a lawn mower, chainsaw or generator by hand pulls a recoil starter. A slow or short pull does not start the engine, and a light machine drags across the ground unless the other hand holds it down, so one arm must brace while the other pulls at speed.
setup: Two YAM arms at the near edge of a wooden table; positions are (x forward from the arm bases, y left) in cm, heights above the table. A starter trainer built like a small engine, which the instruction calls the engine, stands loose on the table: 0.55 kg in all, handle included, balanced over the middle of its base. The base is a grey plate, 20 x 40 x 1.2 cm, of 10 mm XPS foam faced on both sides with 1 mm hardboard, its middle at (35, 20). On it stand a finned dummy engine block, 10 x 14 cm and 13 high, and a housing behind it, 9 x 13 cm and 10 high, both hollow dark grey PLA shells, with steel ballast in the housing over the plate's middle to make up the weight. A black neoprene top pad, 6 cm square and 1 cm thick, is glued on the block, its middle at (35, 12), 14 high. A round red PLA starter cover, 12 across and 3 deep, faces -y at (35, 3.5), its middle 9 high. A yellow polypropylene T-handle sits against the cover on a 4 mm white nylon cord: a crossbar 7.1 cm long along x, 1.9 thick and 2.4 high, centred at (35, -2.4), 9 high, with a thin neck and a socket toward the cover. Handle and cord weigh 50 g. Inside, the cord runs 2:1 round a pulley on the free end of a 200 N/m extension spring anchored at the housing's back, so the pull resistance rises evenly with the stroke: 0 at home, 7.5 N at 15 cm, 15 N at 30 cm. A stop knot ends the cord at 32 cm. There is no engine, flywheel or compression. On the table, a spring scale pulling the unit sideways reads 3.5 N as it starts to slide and 3.2 N while it slides (friction 0.65 and 0.6).
scoring: Measured from a phone video at 120 fps, with a tape on the table and a mark at the top pad's middle. 1.0 when the handle comes out its full 30 cm (5 mm short still counts) within 0.5 s of starting to move, and the top pad's middle never moves more than 10 cm from where it started. A pull that falls short may be tried again once the handle is back home. 0 if no pull reaches 30 cm within 0.5 s, or the top pad's middle moves more than 10 cm at any moment.
reset_notes: Stand the plate back at its marks with the handle home. No seed changes the scene.
fidelity: Rigid-body physics at 240 Hz on GPU. The handle runs on a straight slide with the trainer's 50 N/m at the handle, so an off-axis pull cannot happen. Friction is 0.8 static and 0.7 sliding on the unit, 0.5 on the table, averaged at each contact. No engine: the starter counts as going on the full pull at speed. Unheld, a top-speed pull drags the unit 46 cm. The arm peaks at 1.2 m/s, untested on a real arm: build speed from 0.3 m/s, behind a guard, people clear.
